Police said the fire was continuing to spread at the time of reporting.

The Kotte Municipal Council Fire Brigade has been called in to bring the fire under control. No casualties or the cause of the fire have been reported so far.

title: Sri Lankan war heroes risk being arrested and imprisoned in foreign countries: Joint opposition - Breaking News | Daily Mirror
summary:
Colombo, July 21 (Daily Mirror) - Sri Lanka's military leaders risk being arrested and tried, in terms of the principle of universal jurisdiction, in the national courts of different countries as a result of the investigative mechanism established by the Office of the High Commissioner for Human Rights, the Joint Opposition raised alarm yesterday.

Making remarks during the weekly press conference, its convener, Prof. G.L. Peiris said yesterday that officials of this special investigative body had visited multiple countries and gathered evidence against Sri Lanka's military leaders over serious allegations. They are now processing such evidence, according to him.

"They have been able to gather 96,215 pieces of evidence from 470 sources. According to them, there are 220 witnesses and 250 institutions," he said.

Against the backdrop, he said, Sri Lankan military leaders stand the risk of being arrested, tried and imprisoned in different countries whenever they travel abroad for a holiday, medical purposes, or to attend to the educational needs of their children. He said the countries concerned would invoke the principle of universal jurisdiction.

He said the previous governments, which he represented, flatly rejected the involvement of foreign countries in hearing cases of Sri Lankans in this manner. He said that the then government ensured an internationally acclaimed judiciary in Sri Lanka.

"It was a source of strength for us. As such, we argued against the involvement of foreign courts," he said.

Referring to the government's plan for the extension of the retirement age of judges, he said it had been a move widely opposed by civil society, the Sri Lanka Bar Association, academia and others.

Commenting on the failure to fill vacancies in the higher courts, he said this had resulted in a delay in dispensing justice as a result of a backlog of cases. Earlier, the constitution was amended to increase the number of judges by the previous governments. However, vacancies are not filled today. Does the executive have a hidden agenda behind this move? It is the duty of the executive to fill these vacancies. This will damage the reputation of the Sri Lankan judiciary. The next sessions of the Office on the United Nations Human Rights Council will be held in September this year. Therefore, Sri Lanka could face adverse effects because of the government’s effort to fulfil its vested interests,” Prof. Peiris told a media briefing.

There is uncertainty on the part of the government with regard to the issue. It takes more than one and a half years to implement such a move. They present proposals to people and various groups and gather their ideas on them. There were 1,200 responses for such a move to extend the retirement age of judges within 18 months. We don’t see such a development in Sri Lanka. No one is aware of the government’s move.

Extension of retirement age cannot be confined to judges alone; it should be extended to others, including specialist doctors and academics. There are different ideas expressed on the issue. No idea has been expressed on one matter. It is on that matter which I am going to focus.

title: Fifa opens investigation into Argentina post-final trouble - Breaking News | Daily Mirror
summary:
BBC SPORT - Fifa's disciplinary committee has appointed a disciplinary and ethics prosecutor to assess what happened after the final whistle at MetLife stadium.

Any player or coach involved in the fracas could face suspension, while the Argentine Football Association (AFA) may also be fined.

Following their 1-0 defeat on Sunday, members of the Argentina team and backroom staff were involved in altercations with Spain players as they began to celebrate their World Cup success.

Nahuel Molina, Leandro Paredes, Thiago Almada and assistant coach Roberto Ayala all appeared to be involved.

It was initially reported by Fifa that Paredes had been sent off by referee Slavko Vincic after he pushed Spain's Eric Garcia by the throat.

Paredes' red card was removed from the record shortly afterwards and Fifa has confirmed to BBC Sport that no disciplinary action was taken at the time.

Argentina had already had one player dismissed, with Enzo Fernandez receiving a second yellow card in second-half stoppage time.

Fifa had already begun the process of potential disciplinary action against Argentina after their players held a banner in support of their country's claims to the Falkland Islands following the 2-1 semi-final win against England.

As the final whistle blew in New Jersey, a few Argentina players - including Lionel Messi - slumped to the turf.

Others stood there motionless as Spain's players raced across the pitch in jubilation.

Rodri, who had been substituted in extra-time, ran over from the dugout to join his team-mates.

As the Manchester City midfielder went past Molina, the Argentina defender appeared to punch Rodri on the arm or stomach.

This was the fuse which ignited the trouble.

Rodri confronted Molina, but it was the Argentina player who thrust forward in an aggressive manner.

Garcia ran over to back up his team-mate at which point Paredes got involved too, jabbing Garcia in the throat.

Unused substitute Gavi tried to intervene, only to be forced to the ground by Almada.

Paredes then pushed Gavi to the floor by putting his hand in the Spaniard's face.

Ayala then looked to be holding Garcia around the throat. He then appeared to strike Spain midfielder Dani Olmo.

"Paredes threw two or three haymakers into someone's face. He went for them," Alan Shearer said on BBC One's coverage. "There is no place or space for that.

"We know how much it means to them and we know how much it hurts to lose, but there is a way to lose. Too many times we have seen that from Argentina. The reaction after the final whistle is terrible."

Joe Hart added: "The game's done, they can have absolutely no complaints about what happened today. Disgusting behaviour."

But Argentina boss Lionel Scaloni, who had attempted to calm the situation, appeared to play down the incidents in his post-match interview.

"We are gracious in victory, and we must be gracious in defeat," he said. "Today, we are showing that we know how to lose.

"We lost the match, and we accept it, but that doesn't mean we stop living or forget everything we did to get here."

Fifa's disciplinary committee has a number of options open to it.

By appointing a disciplinary and ethics prosecutor, Fifa will look in more detail at offences rather than just potential violent conduct.

There is a greater chance of stronger punishment if players or the national association is charged and found guilty.

Article 13 of the disciplinary code covers offensive behaviour and the principles of fair play.

The actions of the players and staff could be judged as "violating the basic rules of decent conduct" and "behaving in a way that brings the sport of football and/or Fifa into disrepute".

The disciplinary and ethics prosecutor will take into account "both aggravating and mitigating circumstances", and it has the power to enforce a ban globally.

Fifa used this clause to charge then-Spanish football federation president Luis Rubiales after kissing Jenni Hermoso on the lips after Spain's Women's World Cup final win against England.

Rubiales was banned from all football-related activities for three years in 2023 and lost an appeal to get it overturned.

Uruguay striker Luis Suarez was suspended from all football-related activity for four months for biting Italy defender Giorgio Chiellini at the 2014 World Cup.

It meant the Liverpool player missed the first nine games of the Premier League season.

It is unlikely that Almada, Ayala, Molina and Paredes will face bans as long as this.

The AFA, however, has faced issues with the behaviour of its players in recent years.

Argentina faced charges related to "offensive behaviour and violations of the principles of fair play" and "misconduct of players and officials" following the 2022 World Cup final.

The South Americans beat France on penalties but were criticised for the way they celebrated.

Aston Villa goalkeeper Emiliano Martinez made a lewd gesture with his Goalkeeper of the Tournament trophy, before being filmed in the dressing room mocking France star Kylian Mbappe.

Argentina were fined £18,300 and no action was taken against any player involved.

But Martinez was banned for two games in 2024 for 'offensive behaviour' in World Cup qualifiers against Chile and Colombia.

Martinez repeated his infamous celebration using a replica Copa America trophy following a 3-0 win over Chile. Four days later, he hit a camera with his gloves as a cameraman approached him on the pitch after a 2-1 defeat by Colombia.

Following Argentina's 2024 Copa America win, Chelsea midfielder Enzo Fernandez was forced to apologise for a video he posted. The French Football Federation said the song was a "racist and discriminatory" chant.

At this World Cup, the AFA is already facing a probable fine for the banner held up after the England game.

Their players celebrated while holding a cloth which read "Las Malvinas son Argentinas", which translates as "The Falklands are Argentine".

In 2014, the AFA was fined £20,000 after its players held up a banner with the same message before a friendly against Slovenia.

It is possible that Fifa could issue bans to the players who were holding it: Tottenham's Cristian Romero, former Spurs player Giovani Lo Celso and Manchester United's Lisandro Martínez.

After Spain's 2-1 Euro 2024 final win over England, their captain Alvaro Morata and team-mate Rodri were banned for one game by Uefa after they chanted "Gibraltar is Spanish" during their victory celebrations.

There is no timescale for Fifa's prosecutor to complete his investigation into Argentina's conduct.

On 18 February, Uefa appointed an ethics and disciplinary inspector to look into alleged racist abuse by Gialunca Prestianni to Real Madrid's Vinicius Jr during Real Madrid's 1-0 win against Benfica.

It was over two months, on 24 April, before Prestianni was given a six-game ban for homophobic conduct, with three matches suspended for two years.
